records.question: Can I keep working in Canada while my PGWP application is being processed?
records.gold: Yes, full-time, if you had a valid study permit when you applied, completed your programme, and were eligible to work off campus without exceeding your allowed hours.
records.answer:
Yes—if you meet IRCC’s conditions, you can work full-time in Canada while your PGWP (work permit) application is being processed, including having a valid (not expired) study permit when you submitted, completing your study program, and being eligible to work off campus without a work permit (and not exceeding allowed hours). [S1]
If you received the WP-EXT for PGWP letter, you can keep working until a decision is made even if that letter’s validity period expires. [S3]
If you don’t meet these conditions, you must wait until your work permit is approved (and it’s illegal to work without authorization). [S2][S3]

judge.reason: The answer matches the gold answer: yes, you can work full-time while the PGWP is processed if you meet the listed conditions. Every factual claim is supported by the provided sources, and the citations are attached appropriately.
